description: 4 different engineering field (Chemical, Electronics, Civil, and Software) joins forces to help farmers plant their crops, navigating through the climate, and terrain.
summary: Farmers in climate vulnerable tropical regions such as Malaysia faces unpredictable monsoon shifts, soil degradation, and extreme weather. Satellites data are crucial as it can guide farm planning, but for the average Johan, it is inaccessible. We developed TanamTenang ("Plant Calmly") as an open-source, ecological decision engine that translate NASA Earth observations into a usable farm management, and crop rotation planner. It models 31 agricultural items from annual crops, cover crops, and livestock. Rather than relying on a greedy single-season picks, the engine evaluates 4,096 crops sequence combinations for four rotation strategies: Carry on, Best Return, Build Soil, and Conserve Water. TanamTenang operations is across Sri Aman, Sarawak, Malaysia at 250m grids, and evaluates any coordinates via NASA POWER, and SoilGrids APIs. It runs entirely on your client side browser. TanamTenang equips farmers to adapt with confidence and transparency!
details:
1. What is Tanam Tenang?

TanamTenang or Plant Calmly is an agro-ecological decision support tool built for but not limited to farmers. It requires three simple inputs from the users:

i. Where is your field?
ii. What are you planning to plant?
iii. What matters to you? For example: yield, water conservation, or soil health?

2. How does it works?

i. FAO Soils Engine: We took the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations Soils Bulletin which provide guidance, scientific reviews, and practical manuals on soil science, soil management, land evaluation, conservation, and fertility, and build a land evaluation engine.
ii. Liebig's Law of the Minimum: Scores are determined through a weighted mean, which pulls the final suitability score leaning towards the weakest factor. This is due to conditions such as: Good rainfall cannot compensate toxic soil pH or extreme flooding.
iii. Multi-Season Rotation Planner: TanamTenang searches all 4,096 possible crop sequence to benchmark four strategies of a. Carry On as You Are, b. Best Returns, C. Build the Soil Health, and d. Water Conservation.

3. TanamTenang's Benefits:

i. Zero-Install & Negligible Latency: No backend, no data database deployment, no server round trips. Usable for farmers in rural areas with slow internet.
ii. Variety of Farms: Covers staple food crops, cover crops, aquaculture, and even lifestocks. Important as smallholders often times has a wide ecosystems.
iii. Clear Actions: Clear difference between FAO suitability classes (S1 to S3), and splits unsuitable land with the improvement approaches.

4. Intended Impacts:

Smallholders farmer around the equator are exposed to humid tropics, rapid land degradation, fire risks, and volatile climates that keeps on getting worse under the extreme monsoon season. TanamTenang takes petabytes of Earth observation data from NASA and turns it into a farm decisions machine. It enables communities to understand their land better, moving from destructive monocultures, to diverse crops rotations that can withstand the future climates.

5. Tools, programming languages, and software used:

i. Frontend: Vue 3, TS, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide Icons.
ii. Mapping: MapLibre GL rendering pre-computed raster layers.
iii. Data Ingest: Docker, GDAL, Python.
iv. Hosting & CI/CD: Github Actions & Github Pages.

6. How is it different?

i. Honesty: A missing satellite is marked as null, rather than zero or any assumptions.
ii. "Grid as an Image": Geospatial lattices as binary layers usage enables browser's graphics pipeline and type arrays to be shown very fast.
iii. Multi-Decade Horizon: By taking NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 (which covers climate projections via SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 out to 2070), farmers can plan their plants in advance.

7. Factors Considered:

i. Peatland dynamics (conditions & fire hazards).
ii. Topographic Wetness Index & Height Above Nearest Drainage (HAND) for flood risk.
iii. Evapotranspiration dynamics (calculated via FAO-56 Penman-Monteith equations).

8. Github Repo: https://github.com/lucoslabs-cloud/tanamtenang-spaceapps

___________________________________________________________________________

Super Intelligence (SI) & AI Attribution

Audio & Voice Synthesis: ElevenLabs (used for narration in the project demonstration video). The spoken narration in the 30-second project demonstration video was synthesized using ElevenLabs.

Large Language Models (LLMs): Anthropic Claude & Google Gemini (used for engineering acceleration, algorithmic porting, and documentation refinement). THis was done in the following processes:

i. Algorithmic Porting: Assisting in translating the FAO Soils Bulletin 32 trapezoidal membership equations, Liebig's law calculations, and rotation search logic from the backend PHP/PostGIS platform into client-side TypeScript.

ii. Frontend & Worker Scaffolding: Assisting in scaffolding Vue 3 components, Tailwind CSS v4 styling, MapLibre GL canvas layers, and off-thread Web Worker messaging.

iii. Documentation: Assisting in structuring technical summaries, markdown tables, and editorial refinement of user guides.

What SI Was NOT Used For (Original Human & Scientific Foundation)

i. No Synthetic Earth Observation Data: No climate, elevation, soil, or vegetation figures were generated or simulated by AI. All data originates strictly from official NASA sources (SRTM, POWER, MODIS, NEX-GDDP-CMIP6) and partner databases (ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0, UN OCHA).

ii. Original Agronomic Model & System Architecture: The decision matrix, 4-strategy rotation formulation (Carry On, Best Return, Build Soil, Conserve Water), 343 enterprise requirement envelopes, and "grid-as-an-image" architecture were designed, formulated, and verified by the team.

iii. No NASA Branding Elements: In accordance with challenge rules, no NASA logos, flags, seals, or mission identifiers were created, modified, or generated by SI tools.
